provenance.instrument: West Bradford Township Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 450 Zoning, Ord. No. 1977-1 of 1-2-1977, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 WE3104, Township of West Bradford, Chester County (450-8 LOT: recorded 'in the office of the Recorder of Deeds of Chester County'). Chapter 450 was adopted 1-2-1977 by Ord. No. 1977-1, as amended through 11-24-2009 by Ord. No. 2009-01, with later amendments noted. The accessory suite (450-8, 450-11B(3)(e), 450-12B(2)(d), 450-64H) was added 12-10-2019 by Ord. No. 19-07. 450-64 was last amended 3-12-2024 by Ord. No. 2023-08 and 450-65 on 1-6-2025 by Ord. No. 2025-02. New Laws lists Ord. No. 2026-04 (7-28-2026, Zoning Amendment, Chapter 450): data center definitions and data centers by conditional use in the I/M District (search excerpt). It does not touch the residential rules read here
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 version information: 'Includes legislation through 02-10-2026' (search snippet). New Laws: Ord. No. 2026-04 (7-28-2026, data centers) not yet in the text
checks: An accessory suite is a conditional use in R-1 and R-1C only (450-11B(3)(e), 450-12B(2)(d)), decided by the Board of Supervisors after Planning Commission review, with notice to owners within 250 ft (450-64A). No other district lists it

The suite is attached to or inside the single-family detached house, with one street address, shared utilities (one meter where possible), its entrance inside the dwelling and interior access to all parts of the house (450-64H(2)(a) to (e))

It is for 'employees of the owner of the principal dwelling, or relatives by blood, marriage or adoption', and the property may never be used, advertised or conveyed as more than one independent dwelling unit (450-64H(2)(h))
One off-street parking space for the suite on top of the house's two (450-64H(2)(g), 450-68B(1)). In R-1C every lot needs three spaces outside any garage (450-12G(2))
The code sets no floor area cap for the suite. The definition calls it 'physically subordinate to the principal dwelling unit' (450-8)

A written acknowledgment is recorded before the certificate of occupancy, and the Township may inspect when the house is sold (450-64H(2)(j), (l)). Private deed restrictions still apply (450-64H(2)(k))

R-1 density is one dwelling per net acre and the area figures apply 'for each dwelling unit' (450-11C). The definition calls the suite a 'self-contained dwelling unit', so whether a house with a suite needs two net acres is not settled
More than one principal building may stand on one lot if each meets the lot and yard requirements as though on its own lot (450-61H)
In R-1, extra dwelling units in an existing historic structure are a conditional use on top of the permitted density (450-11B(3)(d), 450-62O)
No accessory building in any front yard or within 10 ft of a street line, and 5 ft between buildings (450-65A)
Front yards depend on the road: the greater of a distance from the right-of-way line and a distance from the center line (for example R-1 local road 65 ft or 80 ft)
Lots developed under the deleted R-1 open space, conventional or TDR options keep the area and bulk rules in force when they were developed (450-72)

R-1C lists the suite among conditional uses that need a tract of at least 200 acres (450-12B(2)(b)) and approval with subdivision or land development plans (450-12N(1)). Whether that reaches a suite on one existing lot is not settled
Single-family semidetached dwellings (a twin or duplex, two dwelling units) are permitted by right in R-3, R-4 and TND-2 (450-16B(1)(a), 450-17B(1)(a), 450-46A(1)(b))
In a Unified Development Area tract with an approved master plan, the R-1 rules apply with the 450-23 changes, and the plan approval replaces a conditional use only for uses the plan names (450-22C)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: West Bradford Township Building, Zoning and Codes. Read in a browser on eCode360, one page at a time, on 2026-11-15, mostly in print view. Searched the code (scope all, which also covers New Laws) for accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, family apartment, ECHO, elder cottage, granny, relative, caretaker, guest house, carriage house, servants, tenant house, living quarters, immediate family, watchman, separate living, cooking facilities, tiny house, second dwelling, caregiver, sleeping quarters and accessory family, then two-family, duplex, double dwelling, conversion, converted, mobile home, manufactured, age-restricted, same general character, one principal, housekeeping, tenant, farm dwelling, accessory unit, second unit and previously repealed, and New Laws (scope law). The first searches missed the accessory suite, which was found by reading the R-1 use list and then searched by name. Read: 450-8 definitions (to SPECIAL EXCEPTION), Article IV (R-1 to R-4) in full, Articles VI (TND-1), VII (R-5), IX (C-1, C-2, C-2A) in full, 450-46 (TND-2 uses), 450-57 and 450-58 (I, IM), 450-61, 450-62O, 450-64, 450-65, 450-68B (on screen), 450-82D (on screen) and 450-5, 450-6 (on screen). Article V (UDA overlay, 450-18 to 450-24) read in full on 2026-11-15. Not read: 450-47 to 450-53 (TND-2 area and design), Article XI, 450-62A to N, 450-63, 450-66, 450-69 to 450-72 beyond the search excerpt, Articles XIII and XV. No section read bars a use variance or unlisted uses. Second pass 2026-11-15: added the R-1C 200 acre tract gate and the 450-12N(1) plan approval, the UDA planned development gate (Article V read in full), R-1 yards for R-4 lots without sewer and water (front included) and the R-1 accessory side yard in the R-2 to R-4 utility rows, and semidetached dwellings in R-3, R-4 and TND-2. The R-1C path is held as a tract gate with a disputed reading, since the tool has no field for a conditional use tied to tract size and plan approval. The density question cites both passages in the note only.

term.note: 450-64H(1) speaks of 'in-law suites and employee housing'

status.note: For employees of the owner of the house or relatives by blood, marriage or adoption, by conditional use in R-1 and R-1C

status_outside.note: No other district lists the accessory suite. R-2, R-2A and R-2B permit 'Accessory buildings and structures customarily incidental to the above', R-3 and R-4 'Accessory buildings and uses customarily incidental to the above uses', and TND-2's accessory list is closed

status_by_form.note: 'An accessory suite shall be attached to or contained in the principal single-family detached dwelling.'

path.note: The Board of Supervisors hears and decides conditional uses after Planning Commission review. The applicant notifies owners within 250 ft and carries the burden of the 450-64A(3) criteria. The Board may add conditions

fallback_path.note: Five findings of unnecessary hardship. Financial hardship is not a basis. No section read bars a use variance

value.name: Second principal dwelling on the same lot
value.conditions: 'More than one principal building may be erected on a single lot, provided that all lot and yard requirements, standards and other requirements of this chapter shall be met for each structure as though it were on an individual lot.' The Zoning Officer requires access suitable for a later subdivision. With public sewer and water the lot needs twice the district minimum, without them two acres
value.note: A second house, not an accessory unit. Two residential buildings on one lot are a land development under the state planning code. Density limits per net acre also apply

value.name: Additional dwelling units in a historic structure
value.conditions: Single-family semidetached, attached and multifamily dwellings 'only through the conversion of existing historic structure(s)'. The added units are 'In addition to the maximum permissible number of lots or dwelling units otherwise permitted'. Rehabilitation to the Secretary of the Interior's Standards, period materials, the landscape setting kept, equipment screened, and a restriction or conservation easement. Lot and yard requirements apply unless physically infeasible

requires.condition: The building is a historic structure (on or eligible for the National Register, or 75 years old with historical or architectural merit, or 50 years old with particular significance, 450-8)

value.name: Single-family semidetached dwelling (R-3)
value.conditions: 'Single-family semidetached dwellings' are permitted by right (450-16B(1)(a)). 450-8: 'A building containing two dwelling units, including a twin or duplex'. With approved public sewer and water: at most four dwelling units per net acre, lot at least 8,500 sq ft, lot width 50 ft per dwelling unit, two side yards of 10 ft, rear yard 25 ft. Without them: one dwelling per net acre and the R-1 side and rear yards for each building. Impervious cover 30%
value.note: A building type. Whether an existing house may be altered into one is not stated. The lot figures are two units at the density per net acre, so land that is not net area adds to them

value.name: Single-family semidetached dwelling (R-4)
value.conditions: 'Single-family semidetached dwellings' are permitted by right (450-17B(1)(a)). 450-8: 'A building containing two dwelling units, including a twin or duplex'. With approved public sewer and water: at most five dwellings per net acre and an average lot area of 7,000 sq ft per dwelling unit, lot width 50 ft per dwelling unit. Without them: one acre per dwelling unit. Impervious cover 35%
value.note: A building type. Whether an existing house may be altered into one is not stated. 17,424 sq ft is two units at five per net acre, which is more than the 7,000 sq ft average a unit

value.name: Single-family semidetached dwelling (TND-2)
value.conditions: 'Single-family semidetached dwelling' is a permitted use (450-46A(1)(b)). 450-8: 'A building containing two dwelling units, including a twin or duplex'. The TND-2 area and design rules (450-47 to 450-53) were not read, so no lot size is given
value.note: A building type. Whether an existing house may be altered into one is not stated. Lot figures not read

building_types.note: 'attached to or contained in the principal single-family detached dwelling'

historic_bypass.note: No historic ADU path found. Historic structures have their own conversion path in R-1 (450-62O)

districts_read_no_listing.note: R-2, R-2A, R-2B, R-3 and R-4 permit single-family detached dwellings and customary accessory buildings and uses but do not list the accessory suite. TND-1 (Romansville overlay) and TND-2 permit houses with their own accessory lists. R-5 permits only attached triplexes. C-1, C-2, C-2A, I and IM permit no dwelling

value.condition: The suite is used only by employees of the owner of the house, or by relatives by blood, marriage or adoption. The property may never be used, converted, advertised or conveyed as more than one independent dwelling unit.

One street address for the house and the suite. They share utilities and, where possible, the same meter. The suite is entered from inside the dwelling, and interior access is kept to all parts of the house. A suite in a basement needs a second exit under the building code.
The applicant shows that the sewage facilities serve the house and the suite adequately.

A written acknowledgment of these rules is recorded with the Chester County Recorder of Deeds before the certificate of occupancy. The Township may inspect when the house changes hands. Deed restrictions, covenants and community association rules that bar suites still apply.
R-1 lots developed under the deleted open space, conventional or transfer of development rights options keep the area and bulk rules in force when they were developed, not the figures shown here.

R-1C lists the suite among its conditional uses, and 'Consideration for conditional use requires a minimum tract size of 200 acres' (450-12B(2)(b)). So in R-1C the suite looks tied to a tract of 200 acres or more, not to one existing lot.

disputed_by.note: The tract rule follows item (a), the smaller cluster lots. The suite was added later as item (d) and 450-64H sets no tract size, so whether the 200 acre tract and the plan approval reach a suite on one lot is not settled

value.condition: In R-1C conditional uses 'shall be approved only in conjunction with the approval of preliminary and/or final subdivision or land development plans', and development must follow the approved plans (450-12N(1)).

If the lot is in a Unified Development Area tract with an approved master plan, the tract is zoned R-1 with the 450-23 changes the plan adopts, not the plain R-1 figures shown. These may include impervious cover of 'the lesser of 6,300 square feet or 1/2 of the lot area', a front yard on a local road of 30 ft from the right-of-way or 40 ft from the center line, side yards of 10 ft (accessory buildings 15 ft unless the house side yard is smaller) and a rear yard of 20 ft. The master plan approval stands in place of a conditional use only for uses the plan names (450-22C), so a suite not named in the plan still needs a conditional use.

types_allowed.note: 'An accessory suite shall be attached to or contained in the principal single-family detached dwelling.' 450-8 also allows 'the conversion of an existing single-family detached dwelling into two units'

max_sqft.note: No floor area cap. The definition requires the suite to be 'physically subordinate to the principal dwelling unit'

internal_uses_district_height.note: Three stories or 35 ft, whichever is less

front_yard_barred.note: 'no accessory building or structure in any district shall be erected in any front yard or within 10 feet of any street line'

max_adus.note: The definition speaks of a dwelling 'with an accessory suite'. No count is stated

spaces_required.note: 'One off-street parking space shall be provided for the accessory suite, in addition to any parking required by § 450-68.'

total_on_site.note: 'Dwellings in residential and nonresidential districts. Two off-street parking spaces per unit.' plus one for the suite. R-1C asks for three spaces on every lot outside any garage (450-12G(2))

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached dwelling: 43,560 sq ft. Lot width 125 ft at the setback line

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: 'Maximum density: one dwelling per net acre'. The area figures 'shall be provided for each dwelling unit'. 450-8 calls an accessory suite 'A self-contained dwelling unit', and a DWELLING UNIT is a 'separate, independent housekeeping establishment' physically separated from other rooms. But 450-64H(2)(e) keeps interior access to all parts of the house, and 450-64H(1) says the suite is not to become a second dwelling unit. So whether a house and a suite need two net acres is not settled
